answer: Arrival-Curve Fingerprinting accepts a new agent identity only if its first-hour activity ramps smoothly like a typical newcomer's plume, rejecting bursts that spike instantly. Genuine use reaches a predictable nadir of early mistakes and hesitations that scripts cannot fake without slowing down. The system mirror-checks each identity's traffic shape against that baseline, so a Sybil farm must either stagger registrations across days or throttle each puppet, paying coordinator time and idle capacity per identity.
